text_blocks.snippet: Can I get a mammogram after receiving the COVID-19 vaccine?
Yes, you can generally get a mammogram after receiving the COVID-19 vaccine. However, there are a few things to keep in mind:
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, you can generally get a mammogram after receiving the COVID-19 vaccine

list.title: Lymph node swelling:
list.snippet: The COVID-19 vaccine can cause temporary swelling of the lymph nodes in the armpit. This swelling may show up on a mammogram.

list.title: Timing:
list.snippet: If you have recently received the vaccine, it is recommended to wait 4-6 weeks before getting a mammogram. This allows the lymph node swelling to subside.

list.title: Inform your doctor:
list.snippet: Be sure to inform your doctor that you have received the COVID-19 vaccine when scheduling your mammogram. This will help them interpret the results correctly.

text_blocks.snippet: Will the vaccine affect the mammogram results?

In most cases, the COVID-19 vaccine will not affect the accuracy of a mammogram. However, the lymph node swelling mentioned above can make it more difficult to interpret the results. If this occurs, your doctor may recommend additional imaging tests.
Getting a mammogram after receiving the COVID-19 vaccine is generally safe and recommended. However, it is important to wait 4-6 weeks after vaccination and inform your doctor about the vaccine.
